examples.en: I left the phone number out of the application.

examples.ko: 메일에 첨부 파일을 누락하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not leave out the attachment in the email.

examples.ko: 제 이름을 누락한 채로 명단이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The list came out with my name omitted.

examples.ko: 중요한 내용을 누락하지 않았는지 다시 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check again that you have not left out anything important.
I am sorry I omitted one thing from the minutes.

examples.ko: 한 줄을 누락할 때가 많아서 꼼꼼히 봐야 해요.
examples.en: I often skip a line, so I have to check carefully.

explain: 일상에서는 '빠뜨리다'를 많이 쓰고, 누락하다는 서류·명단·기록에서 빠진 경우에 써요. 빠진 쪽을 주어로 하면 '누락되다'가 돼요.
explain_en: In daily talk Koreans say '빠뜨리다'; 누락하다 is for things missing from documents, lists, or records. If the missing thing is the subject, use '누락되다'.

en: have a meeting or one-on-one talk with

examples.en: I have a meeting with my homeroom teacher tomorrow.
The team leader met the new employees one by one.
We set a time to meet with the parents.
I was very nervous during the meeting.
After talking with my professor, I decided on my career path.
I met the boss in the afternoon and explained the situation.

explain: 상담은 고민을 말하고 조언을 받는 것에 가깝고, 면담은 약속을 잡고 만나서 이야기하는 것에 가까워요. 선생님이나 상사처럼 윗사람과 만날 때 많이 쓰고, '면담을 신청하다', '면담을 하다'로 같이 써요.
explain_en: 상담 is closer to sharing a worry and getting advice; 면담 is meeting someone by appointment to talk. It is often used with a teacher or boss, as in '면담을 신청하다' (request a meeting) and '면담을 하다'.

examples.en: This song is a classic that has been loved for a long time.
We listened together to the classic songs my father likes.
I bought a collection of that singer's best songs.
Great songs keep being sung even as time passes.
A classic song from the 80s came on the radio.
At karaoke I picked and sang only classics.

explain: 명곡은 오래 사랑받아 온 훌륭한 노래에 써요. 요즘 인기 있는 노래는 '인기곡', 크게 유행한 노래는 '히트곡'이라고 해요. '명작', '명화'처럼 '명-'이 붙으면 훌륭한 작품이라는 느낌이 돼요.
explain_en: 명곡 is for a great song that has been loved for years. A currently popular song is '인기곡', and a big hit is '히트곡'. The prefix '명-' as in '명작' and '명화' adds the sense of an excellent work.

examples.en: The deputy prime minister held a press conference today.
The economic deputy prime minister's remarks were on the news.
The deputy prime minister ranks right below the prime minister.
They say a new deputy prime minister will be appointed.
The deputy prime minister and ministers attended the meeting.
There was a time for reporters to ask the deputy prime minister questions.

explain: 한국에서는 부총리가 경제나 교육 같은 부처의 장관을 함께 맡는 경우가 많아요. 뉴스에서는 '경제부총리'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여 불러요.
explain_en: In Korea a deputy prime minister often also serves as the minister of a ministry such as the economy or education. In the news you hear it with the field in front, like '경제부총리'.

examples.en: I gladly accepted the invitation.
I accepted my friend's request and helped with the move.
Will you accept this offer?
I am thinking about whether to accept the company's terms.
I accepted the apology and we made up.

examples.ko: 입사 제안을 수락하는 데 하루가 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took me a day to accept the job offer.

explain: 수락하다는 부탁·제안·초대 같은 상대의 요청을 받아들일 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '좋아요', '알겠어요'라고 하고, 수락하다는 글이나 공식적인 자리에서 더 자주 나와요. 반대말은 '거절하다'예요.
explain_en: 수락하다 is for accepting a request, offer, or invitation. In casual talk people just say '좋아요' or '알겠어요'; 수락하다 appears more in writing and formal settings. The opposite is '거절하다'.

examples.en: My mother makes white porridge every morning.
I made porridge for my sick younger sibling.

examples.ko: 팥죽을 쑤는 날에는 온 가족이 모여요.
examples.en: On the day red bean porridge is made, the whole family gathers.

examples.ko: 쌀을 불린 다음에 죽을 쑤면 부드러워요.
examples.en: If you soak the rice before making porridge, it turns out soft.
Grandmother cooked paste and put up the wallpaper.

examples.ko: 죽을 쑤고 나서 소금으로 간을 해요.
examples.en: After making the porridge, I season it with salt.

explain: 쑤다는 죽·풀·묵처럼 곡식 알갱이나 가루를 물에 끓여 걸쭉하게 만들 때만 써요. 밥은 '짓다', 국은 '끓이다'라서 동사가 달라요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 시험을 망쳤을 때 비유로 써요. 죽처럼 형체 없이 흐트러졌다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when a test or task goes badly, as if it turned to mush.
phrases.en_equiv: to make a mess of it

explain_en: 쑤다 is used only for boiling grain or flour in water into something thick, like porridge, paste, or jelly. Rice is '짓다' and soup is '끓이다', so the verb changes.

examples.en: Anyway, please come on time.

examples.ko: 그 얘기는 그만하고, 암튼 밥 먹어요.
examples.en: Let's stop talking about that and just eat.
Anyway, thanks, you saved me.

examples.ko: 비도 오고 피곤하지만 암튼 가 볼게요.
examples.en: It's raining and I'm tired, but I'll go anyway.
I don't know the details, but anyway, it's delicious.
Anyway, I'm glad it ended well.

explain: '아무튼'을 줄인 말이라 친구나 가족과 말할 때 써요. 글이나 발표 같은 격식 있는 자리에서는 '아무튼'이나 '어쨌든'이 알맞아요. 앞 이야기를 접고 본론으로 돌아갈 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: 암튼 is a shortened '아무튼', used with friends and family. In writing or formal talks, use '아무튼' or '어쨌든'. It is often used to drop a side topic and return to the main point.

examples.ko: 늦어서 죄송한데 한 번만 양해해 주세요.
examples.en: I'm sorry I'm late, so please bear with me just this once.
When I explained the situation, everyone understood.
The construction is noisy, so we would appreciate your understanding.

examples.ko: 손님이 사정을 양해해 줘서 환불 없이 넘어갔어요.
examples.en: The customer understood and let it pass, so no refund was needed.

examples.ko: 선생님이 사정을 양해하고 시간을 더 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher understood my situation and gave me more time.
It was agreed on in advance, so there was no problem.

explain: '이해하다'는 내용을 아는 것이고, 양해하다는 불편이나 실수를 알고도 넘어가 주는 쪽이에요. '양해해 주세요', '양해를 구하다'처럼 부탁하거나 안내할 때 거의 이 틀로 써요.
explain_en: '이해하다' is grasping the content; 양해하다 is knowing about an inconvenience or mistake and letting it pass. It mostly appears in set phrases like '양해해 주세요' and '양해를 구하다' when asking or announcing.

examples.en: He lived for a long time holding a grudge.

examples.ko: 원한은 시간이 지나도 쉽게 사라지지 않아요.
examples.en: A deep grudge does not easily disappear with time.
A small misunderstanding grew into a bitter grudge.
It is a story about dreaming of revenge because of a grudge.

examples.ko: 그 일 때문에 서로에게 원한이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Because of that incident, they came to resent each other.

examples.ko: 원한에 사무쳐 밤새 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: Consumed by resentment, I could not sleep all night.

explain: 원한은 누군가에게 당한 일 때문에 오래 품는 깊은 미움이라 '원한을 품다', '원한을 사다', '원한을 풀다'처럼 써요. 가벼운 불만에는 쓰지 않아요. '원망'은 탓하는 마음이고, 원한은 갚고 싶은 마음까지 가요.
explain_en: 원한 is a deep, lasting hatred over something done to you, used in '원한을 품다' (hold a grudge), '원한을 사다' (earn resentment), and '원한을 풀다' (settle it). It is not for mild complaints. '원망' is blaming someone; 원한 goes as far as wanting payback.

examples.en: I offered words of comfort to the bereaved family.
The families of the accident victims held a press conference.
The bereaved family received mourners at the funeral hall.
The government decided to support the bereaved families.

examples.ko: 유가족의 슬픔은 말로 다 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The grief of the bereaved family cannot be put into words.

examples.ko: 그 병원에서는 유가족 상담을 해 줘요.
examples.en: That hospital offers counseling for bereaved families.

explain: 뉴스에서는 사고나 재난으로 숨진 사람의 가족을 가리킬 때 자주 나와요. 평소에 내 가족 이야기를 할 때는 쓰지 않고, 위로할 때는 '유가족분들께'처럼 높여 불러요.
explain_en: In the news it often refers to the family of someone who died in an accident or disaster. You would not use it for your own family in daily talk, and when offering condolences you raise it politely, like '유가족분들께'.

examples.ko: 이 작가는 장편 소설을 많이 썼어요.
examples.en: This author has written many novels.
The first long work I wrote won an award.
I like long works more than short stories.
This comic was made as a long work.

examples.ko: 장편의 줄거리를 한 줄로 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Try describing the plot of the long work in one line.
I watched a feature-length animation on the weekend.

explain: 반대말은 '단편'이고, 중간 길이는 '중편'이에요. 소설·영화·만화·애니메이션처럼 이야기가 있는 작품에 쓰고, 노래나 짧은 글 하나에는 쓰지 않아요. '장편 소설'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: The opposite is '단편', and the middle length is '중편'. It is used for works with a story, like novels, films, comics, and animation, not for a song or a short text. It is often placed before another noun, as in '장편 소설'.

en: retake the college entrance exam after a year of study

examples.en: I failed to get into college, so I am preparing a second time.
My friend spent a year preparing to retake the exam.
While retaking the exam year, I went to a cram school.
I am still deciding whether to retake the exam.
After the extra year, I got into the major I wanted.
This time I will study another year and definitely pass.

explain: 대학 입시에 떨어지거나 만족하지 못해서 한 해 더 준비하는 일에 쓰고, 두 번째 도전은 '재수', 세 번째는 '삼수'라고 해요. 일반 시험이나 자격증에는 쓰지 않고 '다시 도전하다'라고 해요. '재수 없다'의 '재수'(운)와 소리만 같고 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is for spending another year preparing after failing or being unhappy with the college entrance exam; the second try is '재수' and the third is '삼수'. For other exams or certificates, say '다시 도전하다'. It only sounds like the '재수' (luck) in '재수 없다'; it is a different word.

examples.en: My older brother finishes his military service next month.
He was discharged two years ago.
After I am discharged, I will go back to school.
On the day he was discharged, his family came to meet him.
He got a job right after being discharged.
I am counting the days until I am discharged.

explain: 군대를 마치고 나올 때 쓰는 말이고 '입대하다'와 짝이에요. 일상에서는 '제대'를 많이 쓰고, 공식 서류에서는 '전역'을 써요. '군대 갔다 오다'도 같은 상황에서 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when leaving the military and pairs with '입대하다' (enlist). In daily talk people say 제대, while official papers use '전역'. '군대 갔다 오다' is also common for the same situation.

examples.ko: 전쟁 때 묻어 둔 지뢰가 아직 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Landmines buried during the war still remain.

examples.ko: 그 지역은 지뢰 위험 표지판이 많아요.
examples.en: That area has many landmine warning signs.
If you step on a landmine, it can explode.

examples.ko: 지뢰 찾기 게임을 해 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever played Minesweeper?

examples.ko: 지뢰는 눈에 잘 띄지 않아서 위험해요.
examples.en: Landmines are dangerous because they are hard to see.
Landmine removal work is very delicate.

explain: '지뢰 찾기' 게임 이름으로도 익숙한 말이에요. 전쟁 때 지뢰를 묻어 둔 곳을 안전하게 치우는 일은 '지뢰를 제거하다'라고 해요. 비유로 '지뢰를 밟다'도 자주 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 민감해하는 이야기를 건드려 분위기가 나빠졌을 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when you bring up a topic the other person is sensitive about and the mood turns bad.

explain_en: Many people know it from the game '지뢰 찾기' (Minesweeper). Clearing mined ground safely is '지뢰를 제거하다'. The figurative '지뢰를 밟다' is also common.

examples.en: I made the inside of the bottle a vacuum.
Space is almost a vacuum.
Vacuum packing makes food last longer.
I cleaned the room with a vacuum cleaner.
Sound does not travel in a vacuum.

examples.ko: 이 보온병은 진공으로 되어 있어서 따뜻함이 오래가요.
examples.en: This thermos is vacuum-sealed, so it keeps heat for a long time.

explain: 생활에서는 '진공청소기', '진공 포장'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 나올 때가 많아요. 과학 수업에서는 공기가 없는 상태로 단독으로도 써요. 뉴스에서는 '권력 진공'처럼 비어 있는 상태를 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: In daily life it usually comes attached to another word, as in '진공청소기' and '진공 포장'. In science class it stands alone for a state with no air. News also uses it figuratively, as in '권력 진공' (power vacuum).

examples.en: The illegally parked car was towed.
My car broke down, so I called a tow.
The towing fee was more expensive than I expected.
A tow truck came and took the car away.
Towing is covered by insurance, so it is free.
A towing operation is going on on the road.

explain: 주로 차에 쓰는 말이라 '견인차', '견인료', '견인되다'로 많이 써요. 고장 났을 때는 '견인을 부르다', 불법 주차로 끌려갔을 때는 '견인당하다'라고 해요. '끌다'는 일상 말이고, 견인은 차를 끌고 가는 일에 쓰는 전문적인 말이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for cars: '견인차' (tow truck), '견인료' (towing fee), '견인되다' (get towed). After a breakdown you '견인을 부르다'; when towed for illegal parking you say '견인당하다'. '끌다' is the everyday word; 견인 is the technical term for towing a vehicle.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 나의 가장 큰 경쟁자예요.
examples.en: That player is my biggest rival.
There are many competitors, so it is hard to get in.
If you meet a good rival, your skills improve.
All the competitors prepared hard.
Sometimes you become friends with a competitor.
I try to learn from my competitor's strengths.

explain: '라이벌'과 거의 같지만, 경쟁자는 시험·회사·시장처럼 같은 것을 두고 겨루는 사람에게 두루 써요. 라이벌은 오랫동안 서로를 의식하는 상대에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: It is close to 'rival', but 경쟁자 is used broadly for anyone competing for the same thing, like an exam, a job, or a market. '라이벌' leans toward someone you have been measuring yourself against for a long time.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 오래전부터 교역을 해 왔어요.
examples.en: The two countries have traded for a long time.
As trade grew, the economy grew.
The port was a center of trade.
The volume of trade is growing every year.

examples.ko: 나라 사이의 교역은 법으로 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: Trade between countries is set by law.
The number of trading partner countries increased.

explain: '무역'이 가장 일상적인 말이고, 교역은 나라나 집단 사이에서 물건을 주고받는 느낌이 강해서 역사나 뉴스에 자주 나와요. '교역량', '교역국', '교역 상대'처럼 붙여 써요. 개인이 물건을 사고파는 일에는 '거래'를 써요.
explain_en: '무역' is the most everyday word; 교역 stresses goods being exchanged between countries or groups and shows up in history and news. It appears in '교역량', '교역국', and '교역 상대'. For individuals buying and selling, use '거래'.

examples.en: We trade rice with that country.
Merchants in the old days traded silk.

examples.ko: 두 나라가 자유롭게 교역할 수 있게 됐어요.
examples.en: The two countries can now trade freely.
More countries trade with one another.
They traded with neighboring countries and shared culture too.
He crossed the sea to trade and became rich.

explain: 나라나 큰 집단끼리 물건을 사고팔 때 쓰고, 보통 '~와/과 교역하다'로 말해요. 일상에서는 '무역하다'가 더 흔하고, 개인 사이에는 '거래하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when countries or large groups buy and sell goods, usually in the pattern '~와/과 교역하다'. '무역하다' is more common in daily talk, and '거래하다' is for individuals.

examples.ko: 화가 나도 사람에게 막말하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even when you are angry, you should not say harsh things to people.
That person speaks rudely to anyone.
I regret saying harsh things to my brother yesterday.
I apologized right after saying those harsh things.
Many people throw rude remarks at each other in the comments.
I spoke rudely to my parents and got scolded badly.

explain: 화가 나서 거칠게 말하는 모습에 쓰고, 욕설이 없어도 상대를 무시하는 말투면 막말이라고 해요. '험담'은 없는 데서 흉보는 것이라 달라요. 뉴스에서는 '막말 논란'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes talking harshly out of anger; even without swear words, a dismissive tone counts as 막말. '험담' is speaking ill of someone behind their back, which is different. In news the noun appears often, as in '막말 논란'.

examples.en: Children imitate adults' behavior.
I copied that singer's dance exactly.

examples.ko: 유명한 디자인을 모방하면 문제가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Copying a famous design can cause trouble.
It is fun to imitate my friend's way of talking.

examples.ko: 다른 작품을 모방한 광고가 논란이 됐어요.
examples.en: An ad that imitated another work caused controversy.
I practiced by first imitating someone who is good.

explain: '따라 하다'가 일상 말이고, 모방하다는 글이나 발표에서 더 자주 나와요. '흉내 내다'는 장난스럽게 따라 하는 느낌이라 달라요. 몰래 베끼는 느낌이 강하면 '표절하다'가 더 가까워요.
explain_en: '따라 하다' is the everyday phrase; 모방하다 is more common in writing and presentations. '흉내 내다' is playful mimicry, which is different. If it feels like secretly copying, '표절하다' (plagiarize) fits better.

en: activation; getting going (as in 'get into gear')

examples.en: I only get going when the exam date gets close.
Everyone got into gear and started working.

examples.ko: 저는 발동은 느리지만 한번 시작하면 끝까지 해요.
examples.en: I am slow to get going, but once I start, I finish.
Some people take time to get going.

examples.ko: 발동도 안 걸렸는데 벌써 퇴근 시간이에요.
examples.en: I have not even got going and it is already time to leave work.
On cold mornings it is hard to get going.

explain: 일상에서는 '발동이 걸리다', '발동을 걸다'처럼 정해진 틀로 쓰고, 일이나 공부가 본격적으로 시작된 상태를 가리켜요. 뉴스에서는 '비상 조치가 발동되다'처럼 제도나 권한이 실제로 작동할 때도 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 처음에는 느리다가 몸과 마음이 일에 맞춰져 속도가 붙었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone starts slowly and then builds momentum once their body and mind settle into the work.

explain_en: In daily life it appears in fixed patterns like '발동이 걸리다' and '발동을 걸다', for work or study finally getting properly underway. In the news it also covers rules or powers actually taking effect, as in '비상 조치가 발동되다'.

examples.en: My mother runs the household at home.
After getting married, I ran a household for the first time.
The husband keeps house and the wife works.

examples.ko: 살림하는 데 생각보다 손이 많이 가요.
examples.en: Running a household takes more work than I thought.

examples.ko: 아이를 키우며 살림한 지 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been five years since I started raising a child and keeping house.

examples.ko: 혼자 살림할 때는 장보기가 가장 어려웠어요.
examples.en: When I ran a home alone, grocery shopping was the hardest part.

explain: 청소·빨래·요리·돈 관리까지 집을 꾸려 가는 일 전체를 가리켜요. 한 가지 일은 '청소하다'처럼 따로 말하고, 살림하다는 전체를 묶어서 말해요. '살림을 차리다', '살림이 늘다'처럼 명사 '살림'으로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It covers the whole job of running a home: cleaning, laundry, cooking, and managing money. A single chore gets its own verb like '청소하다'; 살림하다 bundles them all. The noun '살림' is also common, as in '살림을 차리다' (set up a home) and '살림이 늘다' (accumulate household goods).

en: undergo plastic surgery; shape or reconstruct (the body)

examples.en: There is a rumor that he had his nose done.
I heard my younger sibling gained confidence after having plastic surgery.

examples.ko: 친구는 눈을 성형하려고 돈을 모으고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend is saving money to have her eyes done.
He had reconstructive surgery on his face after the accident.
You need enough consultation before having surgery.

examples.ko: 화상을 입어서 피부를 성형하는 치료를 받았어요.
examples.en: After a burn, I had treatment to reshape my skin.

explain: 보통 '성형 수술'이라고 하고, 성형하다는 그것을 줄여 말한 형태예요. 외모를 바꾸는 경우와 화상·사고 뒤에 몸을 고치는 치료 경우 모두 쓰지만, 일상 대화에서는 외모 이야기로 더 자주 나와요. 남의 얼굴을 두고 '성형했어?'라고 묻는 건 실례예요.
explain_en: People usually say '성형 수술', and 성형하다 is the shortened verb form. It covers both cosmetic surgery and reconstructive treatment after burns or accidents, though daily talk mostly means appearance. Asking someone '성형했어?' about their face is rude.

examples.en: Our family celebrates the holidays together.
We celebrated the birthday quietly with just family.
I went down to my hometown to celebrate the New Year.
The way of celebrating Chuseok differs from house to house.

examples.ko: 명절을 쇠고 나니 몸이 많이 피곤해요.
examples.en: After celebrating the holiday, I feel very tired.

examples.ko: 이사 때문에 올해는 설을 쇠지 못할 것 같아요.
examples.en: Because of the move, I may not be able to celebrate the New Year this year.

explain: '설을 쇠다', '생일을 쇠다'처럼 명절·생일·기념일과 같이 써요. '보내다'는 그 시간을 지낸다는 말이고, 쇠다는 그날의 행사를 챙긴다는 느낌이에요. '생일을 챙기다'와 비슷하게 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It pairs with holidays, birthdays, and anniversaries, as in '설을 쇠다' and '생일을 쇠다'. '보내다' just means spending the time; 쇠다 means carrying out the day's customs. It is often used much like '생일을 챙기다'.

examples.en: The students do their practical training at a hospital.
I practiced hands-on what I learned in class.
The time we practice cooking hands-on is the most fun.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에는 현장에서 실습할 기회가 있어요.
examples.en: This semester there is a chance to train in the field.

examples.ko: 이론을 배우고 나서 바로 실습하면 더 잘 기억나요.
examples.en: If you practice right after learning the theory, you remember it better.
She talked about her experience of student teaching at an elementary school.

explain: '연습하다'는 잘하려고 되풀이하는 것이고, 실습하다는 배운 이론을 실제 현장이나 도구로 해 보는 것이에요. 학교·병원·공장의 수업이나 훈련에 주로 쓰고 '현장 실습', '실습생'처럼 붙여 써요.
explain_en: '연습하다' is repeating something to get better; 실습하다 is trying out learned theory in a real setting or with real tools. It is mainly for classes and training at schools, hospitals, and factories, as in '현장 실습' and '실습생'.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 우호 관계를 이어 왔어요.
examples.en: The two countries have kept up friendly relations.
A delegation visited to strengthen friendly ties.
They held talks with a neighboring country in a friendly atmosphere.
A new friendship agreement was signed.
That team is very friendly toward us.
The citizens welcomed the visitors warmly.

explain: 나라나 단체 사이에서 사이좋게 지내는 관계에 자주 쓰고, 개인 사이에는 '친하다', '친구' 같은 말을 써요. '우호 관계'처럼 붙여 쓰고 '우호적이다', '우호적으로'로 활용해요. 반대는 '적대'예요.
explain_en: It is mainly for good relations between countries or organizations; between individuals people say '친하다' or '친구'. It appears as '우호 관계' and takes forms like '우호적이다' and '우호적으로'. The opposite is '적대'.

examples.en: He met someone at a secluded spot.

examples.ko: 이 골목은 은밀해서 아는 사람만 와요.
examples.en: This alley is hidden, so only those in the know come.
It was a surprise party we prepared in secret.
The plan was very secret.
It was a secret meeting, but the rumor spread fast.
The two exchanged glances that seemed secretive.

explain: 남이 모르게 조용히 하는 일이나 장소에 써요. '비밀스럽다'와 비슷하지만, 은밀하다는 눈에 띄지 않게 몰래 한다는 점을 강조해요. 좋은 일에도 쓰지만 남이 알면 곤란한 일을 말할 때도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is for things done or places kept quietly out of others' sight. It is like '비밀스럽다' but puts more emphasis on doing it unnoticed. It can describe pleasant things, and it is also used for things that would be awkward if others found out.

examples.en: I work as the teacher's assistant.
The assistant organized the documents for me.
I sat in the passenger seat and gave directions.
They say the lab is hiring a new assistant.

examples.ko: 조수의 도움 덕분에 일이 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the assistant's help, the work finished quickly.
The chef's assistant prepares the ingredients.

explain: 조수는 전문가 곁에서 일을 돕는 사람이라 연구실·병원·주방처럼 기술을 가진 사람 밑에서 일하는 경우가 많아요. 자동차 앞자리 오른쪽은 '조수석'이라고 불러요. 같은 소리의 '조수'는 바닷물이 들고 나는 것도 뜻해서 글의 맥락으로 구분해요.
explain_en: A 조수 helps a skilled person, so it is common in labs, clinics, and kitchens. The front passenger seat of a car is called '조수석'. The same-sounding '조수' also means the tide, so context tells them apart.
